text:
Moth and Gravel, Field Note 4. A
control should stay where you

left it. An AI narrated edition
of the published note.

The button was there a moment
ago. You have found the next

action. Your eyes leave the text
and your hand starts toward the

control. Then a picture finishes
loading. The card grows, the

words move down, and the button
is somewhere else. Nothing

dramatic has happened. The page
has not failed. Yet it has asked

you to find your place again.
Decision Docket, our upcoming

product being developed under
Nanavra, had a small version of

this problem in its teammate
card. A decorative portrait

appeared only after its local
image had loaded. Until that

moment, the grid contained no
portrait row. The loaded card

looked right. The journey to
that appearance needed

attention. Make room before the
picture arrives. The approved

portrait was already 64 by 64
pixels. It's arrival added that

height and the existing eight
pixel gap. In controlled

measurements of the actual
component, the following text

and switch control moved by 72
pixels. The fix was a permanent

decorative wrapper in the
portrait's existing position. It

reserved the same 64 by 64 space
from the start. The image still

appeared only after loading. The
card simply knew where it would

belong. No extra artwork was
needed. No animation was added.

The surrounding type, spacing,
and control could remain as they

were. Before, space added on
load, 72 pixels of movement.

Adding a 64 pixels portrait row
and its eight pixels gap moved

the following text and control.
After, space present from the

start. Zero pixels of movement.
The same role pending to loaded

positions stayed fixed at both
tested widths. Explanatory

diagrams, not application
screenshots. The figures

summarize recorded component
measurements at 390 and 1440

pixels for product, partner, and
engineering lead. Pale dashed

marks show the earlier position
or reserved space.

An empty space can be the right
answer. While the portrait is

pending, its place stays blank.
If decoding fails, it stays

blank. The existing error
handling prevents a broken image

from taking its place. That
might seem like an invitation to
add a shimmer, a spinner, or a

message. Here, the image is
decorative. The role and its

description are already
expressed in text. The person

can read the card and use its
control without waiting for the

portrait. A loading treatment
would make the missing

decoration more prominent. A
quiet reserved space gives the

rest of the card permission to
carry on. There is a useful

distinction here. A missing
piece of information may need an

explanation. A missing
decoration may only need room.

Keep the same role in view. The
card lets someone switch between

product, partner, and
engineering lead. An uncashed

role can need another image
load. During that transition,

the old portrait must not
masquerade as the new role. The

existing cleanup and loading
behavior were retained. The

reserved slot does not introduce
a new focus target or an
announcement.

In the bounded keyboard walks,
focus stayed on the real switch

control while the role changed
and the portrait loaded or

failed. The text can still
reflow when the role changes.

Different descriptions may have
different lengths, especially on

a phone. The promise is
narrower. Loading a decorative

portrait for the same role
should not rearrange the work

beneath it. Measure the
interruption you meant to

remove. The comparison mounted
the actual card with its real

local artwork styles and fonts
in an isolated fixture. Delayed

image responses reproduce the
original movement for both roles

at desktop and phone widths.
After the change, the measured

displacement was zero in all
four comparisons. The loaded

arrangement also retained the
same measured geometry. This

matters. Making the pending
state stable did not require a

different finished card.
Failures and cleanup received

their own checks. The appearance
review covered pending, loaded,

and invalid image states across
the two product themes and light

and dark appearances with a
reduced motion case. Those

observations establish a small
component behavior. They do not

establish whole page layout
stability or show how a real

person experiences the full
onboarding flow. That is enough

to make this change worth
recording. An interface contains

many small invitations to spend
attention. Keeping a control

where someone has already found
it is one way to ask for less.

You have been listening to Moth
and Gravel Field Notes. The

written edition is at
mothandgravel.com.
